vehicle.years: 2015 (S550 platform; community sources also report matches on 2016 GT350)
vehicle.notes: Signal meanings below are almost entirely community-reverse-engineered, not from an OEM DBC. Treat every entry as a hypothesis to verify against your own captures unless marked confidence:"verified-on-vehicle".

importantCaveats: vehicleBus values ("HS1", "HS3", "MS") are the PHYSICAL vehicle bus names used by the community sources below -- they are NOT the same thing as CarCANdy's config.json canBuses[].id / CanFrame.bus numbering (1=CAN1, 2=CAN2, 3=CAN3, see Teensy/include/CANManager.h). Which CarCANdy bus number corresponds to which vehicleBus depends entirely on which vehicle bus you physically wired each transceiver to -- fill that mapping into DOC/pinout.md's 'Wired to' table, then translate before using these IDs in CarCANdy config/filters/plugins.

byteIndex is always 0-based (data[0]..data[7]), matching Shared/CanTypes.h's CanFrame.data[8] array -- this is the convention used by ivanyshyn and eturner3's source material directly. The mustang6g_forum_csv source's original Byte_position column was 1-based; it has been converted to 0-based (byteIndex = Byte_position - 1) for every signal below, with the original value preserved in sourceRaw for verification.
Many signals appear byte-identical on both HS1 and HS3 (the two source repos note this repeatedly) -- don't assume a signal is only on one bus just because a source only tested one.

Several ID/byte assignments conflict between sources (see "conflicts" notes on individual signals) -- these are preserved deliberately rather than silently resolved. Verify with the Sniffer page against your own car before trusting either version.

sources.byteIndexConvention: 0-based (explicitly stated: "All byte references start at 0, so the range is 0-7")
sources.vehiclesTested: 2015 Mustang GT Premium / 2016 Ford Mustang GT350

sources.title: mustang6g.com forum thread "Some results of CAN research"
sources.byteIndexConvention: Original column was 1-based (Byte_position); converted to 0-based byteIndex here. Not independently fetchable (403/anti-bot on direct fetch, WebFetch, and a reader-proxy; no Wayback Machine snapshot exists) -- content was supplied directly by the user as CSV, so it could not be cross-checked against the live thread for completeness.
sources.note: 1-based convention inferred by cross-referencing overlapping signals against ivanyshyn/eturner3 (0x230 gearbox mode, 0x2A1 media buttons, 0x083 turn signals all line up cleanly under byte_position - 1).

sources.title: Verified directly on this project's own 2015 Mustang GT via Teensy/src/plugins/ShiftLightPlugin.h
sources.note: Highest-confidence source in this file -- confirmed against real, live vehicle data by the project owner, not just community-reported.

signals.name: lateral_g_relative
signals.notes: Relative to car base -- reads 0 when the car is stationary, unlike 0x092's lateral G which is relative to ground plane.

signals.name: brake_pressure_pedal
signals.notes: Source's own wording: "applied from brake pedal?" -- uncertain.

signals.name: brake_pressure_tc
signals.notes: Source's own wording: "applied also in case of traction control (along with 0x416 b1 bit7)".

signals.name: wheel_buttons_left_bitmask
signals.notes: CONFLICT: ivanyshyn places this bitmask at byte 0. eturner3 reports the identical bit values (0x01=down,0x02=left,0x04=right,0x08=up,0x10=ok) at byte 1 instead (see next signal). Both sources are explicitly 0-indexed, so this is a genuine disagreement, not an indexing artifact -- verify empirically.

signals.name: wheel_buttons_arrows_value
signals.notes: eturner3 sample message: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00. Same bit values as ivanyshyn's byte-0 bitmask above, but reported at byte 1 -- see conflict note there.

signals.name: wheel_buttons_updown_ok
signals.notes: Matches ivanyshyn's byte-0 placement and bit values for up/down/ok (left/right not covered in this row).

signals.name: wheel_buttons_menu
signals.notes: New information not present in ivanyshyn/eturner3 -- back/nav/settings/music menu buttons.

signals.name: steering_noisy
signals.notes: ivanyshyn: "steering with some noise".

signals.name: current_consumption_or_fuel
signals.notes: ivanyshyn guesses "current consumption"; eturner3 guesses "Fuel Consumption??" for the same two bytes. Neither is confirmed.

signals.name: steering_mode
signals.notes: Hex in sources: 0x40 normal, 0x44 sport, 0x48 comfort.

signals.name: turn_signals_bitmask
signals.notes: ivanyshyn: bit4=left, bit5=right (0x10=left, 0x20=right). eturner3 sample: byte0 0x10=left signal (0x50=left signal + flash high beams), 0x20=right signal -- consistent. mustang6g_forum_csv reports 17/33 (0x11/0x21) at the same byte for left/right, ~1 higher than ivanyshyn/eturner3's 16/32 -- likely an extra bit set concurrently, not a contradiction.

signals.name: high_beam_status
signals.notes: Pair of (byte0,byte4) values given together in source; decimal shown, hex: (0,0)=off, (0x40,0x08)=flash, (0,0x10)=switch activated, (0x80,0)=on.

signals.name: high_beam_cruise_byte
signals.notes: Byte topic overlaps eturner3's high_beam_status byte4, but values/encoding don't cleanly match -- unresolved, verify empirically.

signals.name: cruise_cancel_track
signals.notes: "line track press" reproduced verbatim from source CSV -- meaning/spelling not confirmed, possibly Track Apps / Line Lock related given this is a Mustang.

0x084.notes: Looks like a clock/date broadcast (possibly GPS-synced navigation module).

signals.name: day_of_year
signals.notes: Example given: 0x00 0x20 -> 32 -> Feb 1.

signals.name: steering
signals.notes: Possibly redundant with steering signals on 0x076/0x082/0x3A8.

0x092.notes: G-force relative to ground plane (noisy; affected by incline, unlike 0x077/0x213 which are relative to the car body). Formula pattern applies per-axis using that axis's own byte pair -- source text gives one example formula using b1/b2; interpreted here as applying analogously to each axis's pair.

signals.name: lateral_g
signals.notes: Positive = toward right side.

signals.name: longitudinal_g
signals.notes: Positive = toward back.

signals.name: vertical_g
signals.notes: ~9.8 when stationary on a level surface.

signals.name: coolant_temp
signals.notes: eturner3: gauge doesn't move until ~0x80; "freezes" 0xA6 (106C) to 0xC0 (132C) then rapidly ramps and can trigger overheat warning.

signals.name: oil_temp
signals.notes: eturner3: gauge starts moving at 0x60 (36C), caps ~0xDA (158C).

signals.name: overheat_flag
signals.notes: A high byte0 alone can also trigger the warning per source.

signals.name: engine_load_torque
signals.notes: Source: "looks like engine load / torque"; same underlying bytes noted elsewhere as matching 0x42F b4<<8+b5.

signals.name: map_pressure
signals.notes: Manifold absolute pressure guess. Formula reproduced verbatim from source; parenthesis grouping in the original is ambiguous -- verify before using.

signals.name: current_gear
signals.notes: Additional gear values 36/52/68/84/100 correspond to successive gears (1st..5th, exact mapping not spelled out in source) with bit0/bit1 as flags on top.

signals.name: launch_control_icon
signals.notes: eturner3 gives leading-nibble shorthand 0x2_/0x8_/0xA_; decimal values shown are for the nibble value only (low nibble unspecified/masked).

signals.name: unconfirmed_graphs
signals.notes: "some +/- constant graph during run" on b2<<8+b3, b5, b6, b7 -- not decoded.

0x179.notes: eturner3: this message suppresses several dashboard warnings (fuel service inlet, change oil soon, oil change required) -- exact bits not identified.

signals.name: unconfirmed_sawtooth
signals.notes: Saw-like graph during engine off, idle, and run.

signals.name: speed_ivanyshyn
signals.notes: CONFLICT: eturner3 reports a different scale/units for the same two bytes -- see speed_eturner3. Verify which (or neither) matches your car before using.

signals.name: speed_eturner3
signals.notes: Source states the raw value equals speed_mph * 175, i.e. mph = raw/175 (formula here inverted for forward decoding); byte4's leading nibble must be 6 or the gauge doesn't respond. Scale disagrees with ivanyshyn's raw/100 -- see speed_ivanyshyn.

signals.name: rpm
signals.notes: Confirmed in Teensy/src/plugins/ShiftLightPlugin.h against real 2015 Mustang GT data (bus 1 in this project's own CarCANdy bus numbering). Matches ivanyshyn's b3<<8+b4 *2 and eturner3's "gauge is half of actual RPM, 0-4000 range" exactly -- three independent confirmations.

signals.name: accelerator_pedal
signals.notes: 0-100 range per source.

signals.name: current_gear_guess
signals.notes: bit7 drops sometimes during gear changes; bit2 drops sometimes -- not fully decoded.

signals.name: tc_braking_countdown
signals.notes: 255 counts down when traction control applies braking.

signals.name: tc_applied_flag
signals.notes: Works with TC ON and OFF, does not work with ATC OFF.

signals.name: tc_braking_applied
signals.notes: Same underlying signal as tc_braking_countdown (byte 1).

signals.name: longitudinal_g
signals.notes: Relative to car base -- 0 when stationary, unlike 0x092.

signals.name: unexplained
signals.notes: "not understandable saw-like graphs, frequency correlates with speed".

signals.name: current_gear
signals.notes: 32/48/64/80/100 correspond to successive gears per source, exact mapping beyond 1st not spelled out.

signals.name: gearbox_mode
signals.notes: ivanyshyn gives 2=R,4=N,6=D,8=S (byte 1); mustang6g_forum_csv gives 0=parking,2=reverse,4=neutral,6=drive,8=sport at (1-based) byte_position 2 = 0-based byte 1 -- same byte, same values, forum source adds the 0=Park case. Strong cross-confirmation, also confirms the forum CSV's 1-based indexing.

signals.name: headlight_current_guess
signals.notes: "correlates with headlights on/off, saw-like graph when engine idles. Current?"

signals.name: voltage
signals.notes: Smoother than 0x082 b4 voltage reading.

signals.name: wheel_buttons_right
signals.notes: Exact agreement between ivanyshyn (0x32/0x33/0xFD/0xFE/0x44 = prev/next/vol+/vol-/mute at byte 0) and mustang6g_forum_csv (50/51/253/254/68 = same, at byte_position 1 = byte 0) across all 5 overlapping values -- highest cross-confirmation of any signal in this file besides 0x204 rpm and 0x3B5 tire pressure. menu_M/phone_up/phone_down/voice_command/none_pressed are ivanyshyn-only additions.

signals.name: odometer_guess
signals.notes: "constantly grows, depending on speed. Odometer?"

signals.name: accel_pedal_correlated_guess
signals.notes: "smooth inertial graph, correlates with acceleration pedal with some delay".

signals.name: fuel_level_guess
signals.notes: "slowly decreases during run. Gas in tank?"

signals.name: climate_related_guess
signals.notes: "correlates with climate functionality" -- no byte specified.

signals.name: ambient_headlight_flag
signals.notes: Changes 4/2 when ambient light or headlights on/off.

signals.name: alternator_guess
signals.notes: Spikes on engine start.

signals.name: steering
signals.notes: Another steering signal; possibly redundant with 0x076/0x082/0x085.

signals.name: unexplained_transient
signals.notes: 32 -> 33 -> 32 on engine start.

0x3B3.notes: eturner3: if this message is not sent, the instrument cluster will not even boot up when power is supplied -- treat with care if transmitting on this ID.

signals.name: ambient_light_mode
signals.notes: CONFLICT: ivanyshyn/eturner3 agree 0x48=daylight/DRL, 0x88=twilight/night, 0x4A=hazard. mustang6g_forum_csv instead reports 136 (=0x88, the same value ivanyshyn/eturner3 call "twilight/night") as hazard-OFF, and 137/138 (0x89/0x8A) as hazard-ON, at the same byte. These directly disagree on what 0x88 means -- verify empirically before relying on this byte for hazard-light logic.

signals.name: backlight_counter_and_auto
signals.notes: ivanyshyn: counter for +/- instrument cluster backlight buttons in low nibble; 0x1_ = headlamp on non-auto, 0xC_ = headlamp on auto (daylight).

signals.name: backlight_dimming
signals.notes: eturner3's simpler 3-state read of the same byte ivanyshyn describes as 0x0C dashboard-dark-mode / 0x0D-0x12 dimming range.

signals.name: parking_brake
signals.notes: eturner3 reads 0x80/0xC0=on, 0x00=off from the same byte ivanyshyn assigns to the left-turn-signal flag above -- these may coexist as different bit ranges within byte 6 rather than truly conflict; not resolved here.

signals.name: doors_and_hood
signals.notes: eturner3: first hex digit 0/1/2/3 = closed/passenger-ajar/driver-ajar/both-ajar; second hex digit 2=closed, A=hood-ajar. More granular than ivanyshyn's simpler byte-7 bitfield above for the same byte -- likely overlapping/compatible interpretations of different nibbles, not verified.

signals.name: tire_pressure_fl
signals.notes: Raw units kPa.

signals.name: high_beam_status
signals.notes: eturner3: 0x4_/0x5_ meaning unknown; 0x_C=high beams off, 0x_E=high beams on.

signals.name: dimming
signals.notes: eturner3: first nibble 0/4/8/C, second nibble C/D/8 -- pattern not fully decoded.

signals.name: parking_brake_eturner3
signals.notes: eturner3's nibble-based reading of byte 2 (0x0_=off, 0x1_=on).

signals.name: doors_forum
signals.notes: mustang6g_forum_csv's byte_position 2 (1-based) converts to byte 1 (0-based) here -- a DIFFERENT byte than eturner3's parking-brake byte 2 above, so these two signals are complementary, not conflicting, despite both being about this same message ID.

signals.name: brake_warning
signals.notes: eturner3: "Parking Brake On Warning / Brake Fluid Level Low warning".

signals.name: mycolor_rgb
signals.notes: RGB components of the ambient "My Color" lighting.

signals.name: slow_growth_guess
signals.notes: Slowly grows during engine off, idle, and run.

0x40A.notes: VIN broadcast across 3 sequential frames, distinguished by byte 1's sequence number. Example from source: frames C1 00 31 46 41 36 50 38 / C1 01 43 46 38 47 35 32 / C1 02 33 34 31 39 37 FF decode to VIN 1FA6P8CF8G5234197.

signals.name: vin_marker
signals.notes: 0xC1.

signals.name: vin_chars_ascii
signals.notes: ASCII-encoded VIN characters for this sequence chunk (last chunk pads with 0xFF).

signals.name: unconfirmed_graph
signals.notes: Not understandable graph during engine off, idle, and run.

signals.name: brake_pedal_counter
signals.notes: Some bits work as a counter.

signals.name: tc_autobrake_flag
signals.notes: Referenced by 0x07D's brake_pressure_tc signal.

signals.name: warning_lights
signals.notes: eturner3's reading of the same byte as the tc_autobrake_flag bit above.

signals.name: tc_mode
signals.notes: Merged from ivanyshyn (0x0=on,0x8=off,0x18=ATC-off-7s-hold) and eturner3 (0x00=off,0x02=solid,0x0F=flashing,0x80=TC-off-indicator,0x18=ATC-off) -- both describing the same byte, values don't overlap so merged rather than conflicting.

signals.name: voltage_current_guess_1
signals.notes: Smooth saw-like graph during run, changes on engine start.

signals.name: voltage_current_guess_2
signals.notes: Same behavior as byte 2 guess above.

signals.name: current_guess
signals.notes: Opposite to speed: low at idle, grows on engine start, decreases when speeding up.

signals.name: torque_guess
signals.notes: Source: "looks like torque, the same as 0x167 b1<<8+b2".

0x430.notes: Cluster rejects values too far from the currently-programmed mileage (shows dashes instead) -- not freely writable for testing.

signals.name: odometer_km
signals.notes: 24-bit value across 3 bytes.

0x431.notes: Controls transmission warning messages (Adaptive Mode, Indicated Mode, Warming Up, Adjusted) -- exact bit mapping not identified by source.

signals.name: rpm_accel_correlated_guess
signals.notes: b2 and b3 opposite to each other, correlates with RPM/acceleration.

signals.name: opposite_to_engine_load
signals.notes: Opposite to engine_load (b5<<8+b6).

signals.name: brake_pedal_position
signals.notes: mustang6g_forum_csv's byte_position 6 (1-based) converts to byte 5 (0-based) -- the high byte of ivanyshyn's 2-byte braking_pressure signal above. Likely the same underlying signal at coarser (single-byte) resolution rather than a separate value.

0x4C.notes: CAUTION: this ID (0x4C, 2 hex digits) is noticeably shorter/lower than every other ID in this database (all others are in the 0x07x-0x4Bx range) -- possibly a source transcription shorthand or truncation rather than the literal arbitration ID. Verify against your own capture before relying on it; the signal content below (airbag/seatbelt) is otherwise clearly described.
